observations: Photo 0 shows a compact treadmill with a black frame and belt, branded 'FITYBE SPORTS' on the side of the belt.
The handlebar is wrapped in plastic, suggesting it is new or recently unpacked.
A small digital display is mounted on the handlebar.
Photo 1 shows a close-up of the control panel on the handlebar, with buttons including power, speed up/down, and a large yellow button, likely for start/stop.
The control panel has a textured, non-slip surface.
The background in photo 1 shows a retail or storage environment with boxes and other products.

claims.claim: 2-in-1 Dual Function: Handlebar Down: Functions as an under-desk walking pad (1–4 km/h)
claims.evidence: The photos show the treadmill in an upright position, but do not show the handlebar down or the device in use under a desk. The speed range is not visible on the control panel in photo 1, so cannot be confirmed.

risks.risk: The device may not function as an under-desk walking pad when the handlebar is down, or may not support the claimed speed range of 1–4 km/h.
risks.proof: A photo showing the handlebar in the down position with the treadmill operating under a desk, and a clear view of the speed display showing 1–4 km/h.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not meeting the dual-function claim

risks.risk: The treadmill may be damaged or defective, especially since the handlebar is wrapped in plastic and the control panel appears to have some wear or scuffing.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the treadmill in operation, including start/stop, speed adjustment, and belt movement.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly non-functional or with hidden defects

proof_requests: Photo of the treadmill with the handlebar down, placed under a desk, in operation.
Video or photo showing the treadmill running at different speeds, with the display visible.
Photo of the underside or base to check for damage or wear.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a FITYBE SPORTS under-desk walking pad, but the dual-function claim and speed range cannot be verified from the current photos. Hidden risks include non-functionality or damage. Proof is needed to confirm the device works as advertised and to assess its condition.
